display_matrix.caption_tex: DOP-Net inference. (a) Fixed maps form the conventional AFT input and the PWB input, an angle--delay--Doppler (ADD) tensor. (b) Two independent residual branches denoise the CFR and the ADD coefficients. (c) A fixed alignment places both estimates on a common coefficient lattice, where gate $\beta$ fuses them; the ADD features also predict small synthesis-frequency offsets $\Delta$. Fixed synthesis gives $\mathbf H_{\rm phys}$, and gate $\gamma$ combines it with the AFT estimate to give the final CFR. Shapes omit the user/batch axis; tensor grids are schematic.

display_matrix.caption_tex: PWB observation formation. (a) Received pilot blocks contain energy on null tones, whereas the transmitted support is two disjoint combs. (b) Candidate Doppler de-rotation $\mathbf U_q$ mixes neighboring bins before user-pilot correlation, so for $q\neq0$ off-comb bins contribute; masking first would remove them. (c) Energy normalization, delay IFFT with signed-delay selection, Doppler Gram preconditioning, and a spatial FFT form the ADD tensor. Illustrations use $S=4$ and $C=16$; grids and fans are schematic and do not show measured amplitudes.

display_matrix.caption_tex: Coefficient fusion and CFR reconstruction. (a) A fixed projection maps the AFT estimate onto the ADD coefficient lattice, and a learned gate $\beta$ blends the two coefficient estimates. (b) An offset head on the 48-channel ADD features shifts each synthesis frequency by at most half a bin; the fused coefficient values are unchanged. (c) Signed-delay scattering, a delay FFT, and an inverse spatial FFT give $H_{\rm phys}$, and a second learned gate $\gamma$ combines it with $\widehat H_{\rm AFT}$. Each gate applies one real weight to a complex value. Grids and frequency shifts are schematic.

display_matrix.caption_tex: Full-model residual reconstruction. Each branch preserves its coordinate lattice through encoding, per-voxel tokenization, and three serial sparse axial stages in $D_1\!\to\!D_3\!\to\!D_2$ order. Per-sample $\lambda$ gates mix distance and feature graph priors before neighbor selection and four-head additive attention; they do not mix stage outputs. Context is projected back to encoder width and concatenated with the original features. This feature shortcut differs from the final complex residual addition to the coarse CFR or PWB input. AFT and ADD use independent parameters. Lite disables the illustrated attention path.
